title: OmniVia Core Application Contract v1 - request and response envelopes
description: The transport-neutral request and response shape. Authentication credentials are deliberately absent: they stay transport-owned. A `PrincipalClaim` on a request never becomes a `GrantedAuthority` on a response without server-side validation.

OperationName.title: OperationName
OperationName.description: Dot-namespaced operation identifier such as `memory.get`. The per-operation payload catalogue is out of scope for v1 foundations; only the name is contractual here.

RequestMetadata.title: RequestMetadata
RequestMetadata.description: Everything the server needs to route, scope, bound, and audit a request, independent of the operation payload.

correlation_id.description: Groups retries and related requests into one logical operation.

api_version.description: API contract version the caller is written against.

client.description: Self-declared calling client. Not an authorization input.

workspace_id.description: Workspace the request is scoped to.

scopes.description: Scopes the caller is exercising. Scopes narrow authority; they never widen it.

purpose.description: Why the caller is making this request. A rejected purpose is `invalid_purpose`.

deadline_ms.description: Relative time budget for the request. Expressed as a budget, not an absolute instant, so no clock synchronization is assumed.

idempotency_key.description: Makes a mutation safe to retry.

required_capabilities.description: Capabilities this request depends on, with the minimum version the caller can work with.

principal_claim.description: UNTRUSTED caller claim about the acting principal. The server must validate it before it becomes authority.

RequestEnvelope.title: RequestEnvelope
RequestEnvelope.description: A single application request: what to do, under what conditions, with what payload.

ResponseMetadata.title: ResponseMetadata
ResponseMetadata.description: Operation-independent response metadata. Present on both success and error responses so a caller can always negotiate versions and read its own authority, even when the operation failed.

request_id.description: Echoes the request attempt this response answers.

correlation_id.description: Echoes the logical operation this response belongs to.

authority.description: Server-validated authority actually applied. The only authority statement a caller may trust.

job.description: Reference to asynchronous work this operation started.

freshness.description: Staleness statement, for reads served from a projection.

canonical_resolution_time.description: The instant the server treated as 'now' when resolving this operation, so results are reproducible.

omissions.description: Things the caller asked for that were deliberately not returned.

audit_reference.description: Reference to the audit record for this operation.

SuccessResponseEnvelope.title: SuccessResponseEnvelope
SuccessResponseEnvelope.description: A successful response. Carries `result` and never `error`.

ErrorResponseEnvelope.title: ErrorResponseEnvelope
ErrorResponseEnvelope.description: A failed response. Carries `error` and never `result`.

ResponseEnvelope.title: ResponseEnvelope
ResponseEnvelope.description: Exactly one of a success or an error response, never both. Both branches close their property set, so a document carrying `result` and `error` together matches neither branch and is invalid.
